_comment: Phase 6i. The ledger is falling behind the events it is supposed to account
for. Half of phase 6's last exit criterion.
WHY payorch.consumer.lag AND NOT kafka.consumer.fetch.manager.records.lag.max
Both now exist - 6i attached a MicrometerConsumerListener as well, because
the client's own view is free and is what the consumer is reacting to. It is
the wrong one to page on, and for the same shape of reason experiment 07
found in three of four phase-4 rules: it cannot fire for the incident it
matters most for.
records-lag-max is computed BY the consumer FROM fetches the consumer made.
A consumer that has crashed, been descheduled, deadlocked on a merchant's
webhook endpoint, or failed to rejoin its group after a rebalance publishes
no lag at all. The series stops. So the metric goes quiet at precisely the
moment the backlog begins growing without bound, and a `> N` threshold on it
is unfireable for a dead consumer.
payorch.consumer.lag asks the BROKER: end offset minus committed offset,
summed over partitions. True whether or not the consumer is alive.
AND IT IS STILL NOT ENOUGH, WHICH IS WHAT alertOnAbsent IS FOR
payorch.consumer.lag is published by the consuming service, so if that
process dies the gauge dies with it. A lag monitor that shares a fate with
the thing it monitors is half a monitor. The honest fix is an exporter
outside the service - Kafka Exporter, Burrow, or the broker's own metrics -
and until this project has one, silence has to be the alert: absentFor turns
'no data for 3 minutes' into a firing rule rather than into a green
dashboard.
matchType 2 is 'all the time'. A lag spike that drains in twenty seconds is
a consumer doing its job; 'at least once' would page for it. What deserves
waking somebody is lag that does NOT come down, which is what 'above the
threshold for the whole window' means.
evalWindow 2m rather than 5m: at 6 partitions and a normal event rate, two
minutes of sustained backlog is already several hundred payments the ledger
has not accounted for. Note that SigNoz adds its own eval_delay of 2m on top
- see tools/obs/alert-drill.sh for how much that costs a drill.
target 50 is deliberately not 0. Lag is normally non-zero: the relay
publishes in batches and the consumer commits per record, so a healthy
system is a few records behind at any instant.

annotations.description: The {{$labels.group}} group has not committed offsets for a sustained backlog on {{$labels.topic}}. Every lagging event is a payment the ledger has not accounted for yet. If this alert fired with NO DATA, the consumer is not reporting at all - check that the service is alive before checking the backlog.
